title: Retatrutide, a Triple Hormone Receptor Agonist, for Treatment of Obesity.
journal: The New England journal of medicine
excerpts: For weight-related end points, intercurrent events were handled by a treatment-regimen estimand (intention-to-treat [ITT]).
the corresponding changes in the pain score in the retatrutide groups for the hybrid estimand were -3.2, -3.5, and -3.6 versus -1.9 with placebo
for the hybrid-treatment estimand were -22.9, -34.3, and 31.7 versus -9.9 (differences, -24.4 and -21.9; both P<0.001)
The mean percent change in body weight in the retatrutide groups was -17.6% (4-mg dose), -23.7% (9-mg dose), and -25.0% (12-mg dose) versus -3.9%
(differences, -19.8 and -21.0 percentage points, respectively; P<0.001 for both comparisons)
Retatrutide is a triple-receptor agonist of glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide, glucagon-like peptide-1, and glucagon receptors.
